prayer noun

also prayers, a prayer

classical

Cic. Planc. 97: eōrum precēs et vōta exaudiēns (Lewis & Short)
Ambr. hymn. Deus creātor 10

precēs, precum f. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

prayer, prayers (to God)

The classical word for prayer to God or the gods, nearly always plural; the singular lives on in the ablative prece (Hor., Ov.). To say one’s prayers is precēs dīcere (Schottennius) or recitāre (Vives).

Other words

  • ōrātiō, ōrātiōnis f. — a prayer; prayer

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Act. 1.14: erant persevērantēs ūnanimiter in ōrātiōne; Vulg. Jac. 5.15

    Classically a speech; in the Vulgate and the Church a prayer, and prayer itself (Lewis & Short), as in Ōrātiō Dominica, the Lord’s Prayer.

  • precātiō, precātiōnis f. — a prayer, a set form of prayer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 1: sollemnis comitiōrum precātiō (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. Lord's Prayer

    One prayer or its set words; the school dialogues call the Lord’s Prayer precātiō Dominica (Vives, Corderius; Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • grātēs perāctō jam diē et noctis exortū precēs

    thanks, now the day is done, and prayers as night comes onAmbr. hymn. Deus creātor 9–10

  • Porcōrum est edere, nūllīs precibus dictīs.

    Eating without saying grace is for pigs.Schott. Conf., Ante et post cibum hymnum esse dīcendum

  • et ōrātiō fideī salvābit īnfirmum

    and the prayer of faith will save the sick manVulg. Jac. 5.15

See also pray, the Lord’s Prayer, amen, give thanks, kneel.
